exposure: Bilateral Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block with 20 ml 0.75% ropivacaine
outcome: Adverse effects (inadequate uterine contractions, uterotonics administration)
cohort: 250 patients undergoing elective or emergency Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS) were included in the study.
finding: 0.75% ropivacaine in TAP block provided better analgesia with lower VAS scores and longer duration, and had a better safety profile compared to intramuscular diclofenac for post-caesarean pain.
followup_time: Up to 20 hours post-operation for analgesia duration, with observation for rescue analgesia within 12 hours.
